100 m wide with a 44 m drop into the Jökulsárgljúfur canyon.
xQ1130718: A waterfall on the Skógá River in southern Iceland, at the cliffs marking a former coastline.
The ancient sea cliffs now stand about 5 km inland, forming a border between the coastal lowlands and the Icelandic Highlands.
xQ214924: The most powerful waterfall in Europe, on the High Rhine between the Swiss cantons of Schaffhausen and Zurich.
150 m wide and 23 m high, with summer water flow more than double the winter average.
A popular tourist attraction close to the border with Germany.
xQ639731: Austria's highest waterfall, on the Krimmler Ache river in the High Tauern National Park, Salzburg.
Has a total height of 380 m.
xQ491677: The highest waterfall in Yosemite National Park, dropping 739 m in total, a major attraction especially in late spring.
xQ223649: A complex of seasonal waterfalls in South Africa's Drakensberg range, among the contenders for the world's tallest waterfall.

Fed by the Tugela River, which rises on the Mont-Aux-Sources plateau.
xQ38408: One of New Zealand's tallest waterfalls, near Milford Sound on the South Island.

xQ983252: A pair of waterfalls on the Quây Sơn River straddling the China-Vietnam border.

xQ38161: The widest waterfall in the world, on the Mekong River in southern Laos near Cambodia.

xQ672241: A segmented waterfall on the Sharavati River in Karnataka, India, plunging about 253 m into four distinct cascades.

xQ1266055: A waterfall on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia's Amhara Region, known locally as Tis Abay, meaning 'great smoke'.

xQ495475: A waterfall on the White Nile in Uganda, where the river squeezes through a 7 m gap before tumbling 43 m into Lake Albert.

xQ38432: The largest waterfall in China, on the Liuzhi River in Guizhou province.

xQ512389: A two-tiered waterfall in Peru's Amazonas region, not widely known outside the area until a 2002 expedition brought it to international attention.

xQ38417: A series of seven cataracts along the Lualaba River in the DR Congo, formerly known as Stanley Falls.

xQ798283: The tallest waterfall in both Tanzania and Zambia, on the border of the two countries near Lake Tanganyika.

xQ37319: The tallest waterfall in Oregon, dropping in two tiers over basalt cliffs in the Columbia River Gorge.

xQ3361971: One of the tallest waterfalls in Europe and the eighth-tallest in the world, in Norway's Møre og Romsdal county.

xQ183395: A waterfall in Switzerland's Bernese Oberland, famous as the setting for Sherlock Holmes's fatal confrontation with Moriarty in Arthur Conan Doyle's 'The Final Problem'.
xQ38580: The tallest man-made waterfall in the world, created by the Romans in 271 BC near Terni, Italy.
xQ686835: A waterfall near Lauterbrunnen in Switzerland's Bernese Highlands, dropping 297 m from a hanging valley.

xQ1101379: A waterfall on the Kunene River in northern Namibia, 120 m high and up to 700 m wide in full flood.
Among the largest waterfalls in Africa by both volume and width.
xQ37545: A four-tiered waterfall on the Mahadayi River in Goa, India, among the country's tallest waterfalls.
Its name means 'Sea of Milk' in reference to its frothy appearance.
xQ40417: A waterfall on Stony Creek in Queensland's UNESCO-listed Wet Tropics, Australia's tallest single-drop waterfall at 268 m.
xQ5683183: A waterfall on Havasu Creek within the Grand Canyon, Arizona.
xQ1635297: A waterfall on the Snake River in Idaho, nicknamed the "Niagara of the West" for being taller than Niagara Falls.

xQ602973: The largest waterfall on China's Yellow River and the world's largest yellow-coloured waterfall.

xQ19558: A massive rapid on the Congo River near Matadi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with one of the highest water discharges of any waterfall on Earth.
Site of the Inga I and Inga II hydroelectric dams, with the planned Grand Inga Dam envisioned as the world's largest power producer.
xQ278245: The world's largest glacier, in East Antarctica, draining 8% of the Antarctic ice sheet northward to the Amery Ice Shelf.
About 96 km wide and over 435 km long, named in 1957 after Australian mapping director Bruce Lambert.
xQ367943: A major glacier in Argentine Patagonia, one of 48 fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, the world's third-largest reserve of fresh water.
A top tourist attraction, named after explorer Francisco Moreno, who helped settle the Andean border dispute between Argentina and Chile.
xQ204658: The largest glacier in the Alps, in Switzerland's Bernese Alps, formed by four smaller glaciers converging at Konkordiaplatz.
Part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO World Heritage Site, it has been rapidly retreating, losing 3.2 km of length since 1870.
xQ684169: The longest glacier in Austria and the Eastern Alps, lying beneath the Grossglockner.
About 8.4 km long, within the High Tauern mountain range.
xQ333946: The longest glacier in the Karakoram and second-longest outside the polar regions, in Indian-administered Ladakh.

xQ631789: The longest glacier in the world outside the polar regions, in Tajikistan's Pamir Mountains.
Extends about 77 km and reaches up to 1,000 m thick.
xQ805806: A glacier in Pakistan's Karakoram range, surrounded by some of the world's highest peaks including K2.
Rather than retreating like many glaciers, research shows it experiences surges and shifts into neighboring ice flows.
xQ855226: A glacier in the Karakoram range in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan, one of the largest in the entire range.
Flows southeast from the central Karakoram crest; its accumulation zone of permanent snow and ice makes up 68% of its total basin area.
xQ770424: A major outlet glacier in West Greenland near Ilulissat, draining 6.5% of the Greenland ice sheet.

xQ1632936: A glacier spanning Wrangell-St. Elias National Park in Alaska and Kluane National Park in Yukon, Canada.
xQ583591: A valley glacier on the northern slopes of the Mont Blanc massif in the French Alps.

xQ673150: A temperate maritime glacier on New Zealand's South Island, descending from the Southern Alps within Te Wāhipounamu World Heritage Site.
Lies alongside the Fox Glacier about 20 km to the south; its terminal feeds the Waiho River.
xQ7799533: A vast, fast-flowing Antarctic glacier nicknamed the 'Doomsday Glacier' for its potential to raise global sea levels.

xQ1920336: A glacier near Juneau, Alaska, within the federally protected Mendenhall Glacier Recreation Area in the Tongass National Forest.

xQ391165: One of six glaciers flowing from the Columbia Icefield in the Canadian Rockies, the most visited glacier in North America.

xQ691557: A major source of the Ganges, in Uttarakhand, India, near the Tibetan border.

A traditional Hindu pilgrimage site, with devotees trekking to bathe in its icy waters.
xQ1434582: A glacier in the Himalaya of southern Tibet, fed by Mount Everest and flowing north through the Rongbuk Valley.
Home to the Rongbuk Monastery at its northern end, the highest monastery in the world.
xQ654352: The largest glacier in continental Europe, in Vestland county, Western Norway.
Its highest peak, Lodalskåpa, reaches 2,083 m.
xQ617835: The largest piedmont glacier in the world, in southeastern Alaska, roughly the size of Rhode Island.
xQ1514989: Antarctica's fastest-melting glacier, responsible for about 13% of the continent's ice loss.
Its drainage basin contributes more ice to the sea than any other on Earth, with large icebergs calving almost yearly since 2015.
xQ962630: A large valley glacier on Argentina's Southern Patagonian Ice Field, within Los Glaciares National Park.
